Return exactly one JSON object satisfying the named schema, without markdown fences. Give public derivations only; never provide private hidden reasoning. Do not score, rank or optimize the material. You may answer cannot_decide only by naming the specific missing derivation. Do not manufacture a claim, objection, check or result to satisfy the schema. This is the r003-open-v1 profile. The working_position relation is public bookkeeping, not an oracle, score, correctness test, or semantic stopping rule. Critic fork branch_point_id values are participant labels for a real answer step located under R3-A2, not investigator answers. Under amendment R3-A1, an accepted decomposed step must end in an explicit public commitment that a check or counterexample could contradict. The schema records the participant's proposed value, relation, or decision and its stated falsifier; this mechanical shape does not establish that the commitment is substantively refutable, true, explanatory, or adequate. Amendment R3-A2 treats an open-problem prose paragraph as a public derivation step. A fork may locate that real step either by its explicit step_index with an empty step_quote, or by a normalized quotation of at least 40 characters from the named step. Normalization folds case, whitespace, and straight or curly quotation marks; it does not license invented text.
Criticize only the quoted CURRENT STEP against the PROBLEM and accepted dependencies. Every objection must locate that current step derivation as its fork step, assign a stable nonempty participant branch label bound to that exact step locator, and carry one finite check the return can redo. Do not criticize later unattempted plan steps or manufacture an objection. Limit working to 6000 characters and objections to at most three. Return an empty objections list when none survives. If a needed check cannot be specified because a derivation is missing, return cannot_decide and name it. Schema: tested-objection-r3-a2.schema.json. A prose counterexample or argued distinction is valid content for a derivation_step check; it need not be host executable. Schema and locator validity establish only public shape and custody, never whether the criticism bears substantively on the step. For each fork, either set step_quote to the empty string and give the exact step_index, or quote at least 40 characters from that step. Reflowed whitespace, case, and straight/curly quote forms are accepted after normalization. A nonempty fabricated or paraphrased quote is invalid even when step_index is valid. Judge only the CURRENT PLAN STEP against the problem and already accepted dependencies. Do not criticize it merely because later planned steps, controls, or whole-problem synthesis have not yet been performed.

BEGIN PROBLEM (479 UTF-8 bytes; sha256=c3a2f3b26662a124c271220ffed79c0c70c834c3acf74de1cfaab6d0a95dbb66)
In a hypothetical experiment, two microbial communities have the same measured species abundances immediately before a heat pulse. One community was exposed to earlier heat pulses; the other was not. After the new pulse, the previously exposed community recovers its measured activity faster. Explain what produced this difference and propose the next investigation that would most help us understand it. The measurements described here are all the evidence currently available.

END PROBLEM

{"depends_on":[],"goal":"Explain the faster recovery by identifying a prior-exposure legacy not visible in measured abundances, and choose the most discriminating next investigation.","step":1}
END CURRENT PLAN STEP

{"commitments":[{"check_or_counterexample":"If exposed and naive communities show no differences in strain-level genotypes, gene or protein expression, heat-shock phenotypes, or interaction assays immediately before the new pulse, this relation is contradicted.","claim":"Faster recovery in the previously exposed community is caused by a prior-exposure legacy not captured by equal measured species abundances, such as within-species physiological/strain-level differences or altered community interactions.","kind":"relation"},{"check_or_counterexample":"If this investigation cannot distinguish transient acclimation from heritable strain sorting, or if the recovery advantage disappears when communities are reconstituted from the same measured species abundances, then the decision is contradicted or inadequate.","claim":"The most helpful next investigation is to combine strain-resolved metagenomics/metatranscriptomics with isolate-level heat-tolerance assays and a reciprocal transplant/common-garden or memory-decay time course before and after the new pulse.","kind":"decision"}],"derivation":"The problem states that measured species abundances are equal immediately before the new heat pulse. Thus any faster recovery in the previously exposed community cannot be attributed to the measured abundance profile. The remaining possibilities are sub-abundance biological differences: within-species physiological acclimation or epigenetic memory, selection for heat-tolerant strains/genotypes, or altered community interactions or extracellular environment. Because the available evidence cannot distinguish these, the most helpful next investigation is one that measures within-species and functional differences before and after the pulse while also testing whether any advantage persists in a common garden or decays without further heat selection. A combined strain-resolved metagenomic/metatranscriptomic survey plus isolate-level heat-tolerance assays and a memory-decay/reciprocal-transplant arm would separate transient plasticity from heritable selection and environmental carryover.","result":"The difference is most plausibly produced by a cryptic prior-exposure legacy—within-species acclimation, strain-level sorting, or modified community interactions—not by the equal measured species abundances. The most helpful next investigation is a strain-resolved functional profiling and common-garden/transplant experiment with a memory-decay arm.\nCOMMITMENT: The most helpful next investigation is to combine strain-resolved metagenomics/metatranscriptomics with isolate-level heat-tolerance assays and a reciprocal transplant/common-garden or memory-decay time course before and after the new pulse.","step":1}
END CURRENT STEP
